newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African interest charges crackdown looming.
newsitem.headline: S.African interest charges crackdown looming.

text.p: Maximum interest rates for credit schemes and more effective policing of the Usury Act were being considered to crack down on excessive interest rate charges, Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin said on Wednesday.

Speaking in parliament, he said that government was increasingly concerned that financial institutions and money lenders were charging excessive interest rates, increasingly leading to the repossession of goods.

"I do believe that it will be necessary to set maxima for interest rate charges irrespective of how an interest rate may be determined, particularly since the prospects for abuse in hire purchase agreements is very high," he said.

His department had also been working with provincial government to improve the administration of the department's commercial arm, revise the Usury Act to improve consumer protection and set up a more effective inspectorate and a more rapid prosecution where warranted.
Erwin said his department was currently investigating more than 100 cases in which financial institutions and money lenders overcharged clients on interest in contravention of the Usury Act.

He said overdraft accounts, credit card schemes, mortgage bonds, mutual finance schemes, agricultural co-operatives, auction sales schemes, personal loans, revolving credit schemes, mail order schemes and participation bonds schemes were being investigated.
Part of the problem was that many consumers did not know their rights and he was also considering a more effective education programme.

Among the abuses uncovered included the levying of sundry charges such as telephone and telegram charges, the capitalisation of finance charges on a monthly rather than a yearly basis and the capitalisation of finance charges on arrear amounts.
